chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The wife may eat and give charity, and the friend may eat in the house of his brother and give charity.

key_terms.أَخِيهِ: His brother (often used for close friend/companion)

ai.seo_question: Does a wife need her husband's permission to give charity or eat from her own wealth?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the financial autonomy of women and the rights of close companions within domestic spaces. It establishes that a wife’s right to consume and donate from her own wealth is independent of her husband’s consent, while a 'sadiq' (intimate friend) enjoys similar privileges in his brother's home, reflecting the Shia legal principle of *tamalluk* (ownership) and the ease of social hospitality.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The wife is that she eats and that she gives charity, and for the friend is that he eats in the house of his brother and gives charity’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Jamil ibn Darraj who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
A woman can eat and give charity and a friend can eat and give charity from the house of his brother.’”
